Use imagery and figuratively rich writing styles.

As a gust whispers its breath into a nearby willowed meander in a place once so utterly mundane yet somehow familiar to an old hand of life's meanders—where one foot has followed one path so oft before—the sun’s warm embrace and golden hue, a painter of skies in all manner from dawn blush and dusk crimson through all of its myriad mottlings of twilight's touch and light—embrakes all the familiar nook's no less intimate, yet subtly different.

The trees that line this path stand in silent sentinel with bark that's worn by seasons past to hues that tell tales in each flayed, textured crease and ridge as the bark whispers of a past unyieldable, a testament that the years of time's passing cannot easily erode; nor do they fade to mere shadows on some old parchment that time itself had long conspired in blunting and dull.

A familiar stone, one so often overlooked or perhaps just now found anew beneath the weight-laden feet as one tramped down that worn, beaten track with each heel striking and sinking, a stone so worn and smoothed with a history and stories
